newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish debt yields drop on renewed EMU confidence.
newsitem.headline: Swedish debt yields drop on renewed EMU confidence.

text.p: Swedish yields fell on Monday and the crown firmed against a generally softer mark.

The market was were optimistic after the European Union finance ministers' meeting at the weekend where an agreement was reached on, among other things, the stability pact which reinforced hopes on EMU starting on time.
"All foreign markets performed well today. Chancellor Kohl's decision to take part in the next election and the ECOFIN-meeting were positive especially for the high yielders," one dealer said.
The crown did not, however, strengthen on its own.
Helped by a generally stronger dollar and weaker mark, the crown firmed to 4.5170 to the mark from 4.5370 late Friday.

"The crown is still in a negative trend," one dealer said expecting the crown to trade between 4.50-4.56. "The problem is the crown is not linked to the ERM mechanism and is not supported at set levels by a central bank."
The Riksbank holds a repo tender at 0730 GMT Tuesday but the market was not expecting a change from 4.10 percent.
Six month T-bill rates dropped eight basis points to 4.15 percent and the ten year bond yield fell 17 to 7.26 percent.
